title_vi: Web 1.0, 2.0 và 3.0: ai giữ dữ liệu, ai kiếm tiền

claims.claim_vi: Web 1.0 (1991 to 2004) was a catalog of static pages browsed by following hyperlinks, with no interaction with the content.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Web 2.0 (2004 to now) brought search engines, social media and recommendation-driven apps; because apps digitalize human behaviour and persist user data, big companies use it for advertisements, one of the main business models.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Web 3.0 (Read Write Own) is an idea much discussed because of blockchain and decentralized apps: creators' content is stored on IPFS and owned by users; apps that want the data must get the user's authorization and pay for it; the change in ownership may lead to major innovations.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source does not say outright that Web 3.0 has no ads; the lesson derives the link between ads and data ownership from the source's statements and marks it as the author's reasoning.
claims.verified_by: Author's reasoning from the source; not checked elsewhere.

claims.claim_vi: IPFS finds files by their content rather than by the location of one server (author's general knowledge, not in the source).
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against IPFS documentation.

design_notes_vi: Ba chặng nối nhau theo thời gian rồi một khung hỏi lại câu của tiêu đề nguồn. Khung cuối nói rõ đó là ý tưởng, để người đọc không coi Web 3.0 là việc đã xong.
source_deviations: The source's title asks why Web 3.0 has no ads but its body never answers directly; the lesson derives an answer from the source's own statements and labels it as reasoning.
The lesson adds that Web 3.0 is an idea under discussion (the source says "the idea has been discussed a lot recently") and that it does not describe a finished state.
IPFS is explained from general knowledge; the source only says content is stored on IPFS and owned by users.
